keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Trent row). The page gives no area: 'roughly corresponding to the present-day Northern Italian autonomous province of Trentino'. The gazetteer's Trento province is about 5,300 km2 (cells). The page notes the principality was reduced to an enclave by the peace of 1516 with Venice and that Ferdinand I occupied Rovereto and declared the Confederation Treaty over in 1567, with no land or years that can be drawn, so the outline stays soft.

ledger.note: 1027: the prince-bishopric. 'By 1027 the prince-bishopric was established by Conrad II' (infobox: separated from Verona in 1027).

June 1511: a perpetual confederate. 'In June 1511 the two principalities of Trento and Brixen received the status of perpetual confederate states among Austrian possessions.' Entered as a protectorate-like tie to the Habsburgs; it lasted to 1803.

1803: secularised. 'The prince-bishopric in 1803 was secularized' and became a principality in the County of Tyrol (Austrian crown land from 1804); 'with Tyrol it was annexed by the Kingdom of Bavaria' in 1805 (the infobox gives the dissolution of the Empire on 6 August 1806; the lead: 'existed until 1803').

certainty.note: The page gives no area or boundary; the modern province is a stand-in and the losses of 1516 and 1567 are undrawn.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Trent row (the lands sit in Holy Roman Empire Minor States).

SCOPE. 1027 to 1803. The page also dates: the killing of Bishop Adelpreto at Arco (20 September 1172, by the Castelbarco lords); the deposition of the bishops by Frederick II (1236); Margaret Maultasch ceding her lands to Rudolf IV of Austria (1363, Tyrol, not Trent); the war of 1509 with Venice, the peasant war 1525-1526, the bombing of Trent in September 1703 and the Napoleonic invasion of 1796. Under Bishop Clesio (1514-1539) 'the seignory of Castelbarco and Rovereto' was gained, undated; 1516 'reduced the principality to an enclave'; Ferdinand I occupied Rovereto and 'in 1567 [declared] the Confederation Treaty over'. None can be placed within the pages' information, so no region events are entered for them.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No area; (2) the 1511 'perpetual confederate' status is read as a light vassalage and may be only an alliance; (3) the end: the lead says 1803, the infobox the Empire's end in 1806.
